Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Money, work & business

organization noun

an organized body: an association, a company, an institution

also organisation, organizations, organisations, association, body (an organization), institution, institutions, institutional

classical

Cic. Sest. 32: nūlla Rōmae societās vectīgālium, nūllum conlēgium aut concilium
Cic. Planc. 32: maximārum societātum auctor

societās, societātis f.

noun, third declension

an association formed for a common purpose; a company

Lewis & Short: union for a common purpose, not a mere gathering; also a partnership, and a company of tax-farmers or traders.

Other words

  • collēgium, collēgiī n. — a body of colleagues or members: a guild, a college, a corporation

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Liv. 2.27.5: mercātōrum collēgium īnstituere; Cic. Sest. 32

    Lewis & Short: persons united by the same office or calling, or living by common rules.

  • cōnsociātiō, cōnsociātiōnis f. — an association, a union

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.157: cōnsociātiō hominum atque commūnitās (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. organization, society, association

    Classically the abstract union of people (Cicero); Morgan–Owens takes it, from twentieth-century Church Latin, for an organization.

  • sodālitās, sodālitātis f. — a society, a club

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. organization, society, association

    See society, an association.

See also society, group, member, office, president.
